headline: Russian satellite closes to within miles of US radar satellite aiding Ukraine
summary: Russia's Cosmos 2612 satellite moved from about 200 miles away to roughly three miles from ICEYE-X36, a U.S.-owned radar satellite that aids Ukraine. A second report cites an expert describing the approach as extreme proximity after the satellite closed in from hundreds of kilometers away.

claims.statement: Russia's Cosmos 2612 (also called Kosmos 2612) satellite maneuvered into extreme proximity with ICEYE-X36, a US-owned radar satellite used to aid Ukraine.

sources.quote: Russian military satellite closes from 200 miles to 3 miles of US radar craft aiding Ukraine
Russian spacecraft maneuvers in "extreme proximity" to satellite used by Ukraine

claims.statement: Tom's Hardware reports the satellite moved from more than 200 miles away to about three miles from ICEYE-X36.

sources.quote: Russia’s Cosmos 2612 moved from more than 200 miles to about three miles from ICEYE-X36, a U.S.-owned radar satellite.

claims.statement: Ars Technica quotes a source describing the maneuver as closing from hundreds of kilometers away to extreme proximity.

sources.quote: Kosmos 2612 closed from hundreds of kilometers away to extreme proximity to ICEYE-X36.
